h1: Lima Coco Resort — Ao Prao Beach on a lighter budget than the luxury resorts on the same bay
intro: Ao Prao sits on the western shore of Koh Samet, a small quiet bay known for clear water and lovely sunsets · Only a few resorts share it, and most are high-priced luxury places — Lima Coco Resort is the clearly more affordable option, a 3-star resort of colourful villas climbing the hillside above the sea, with a beachfront pool and water you can snorkel coral in right off the sand · Rates start at around ฿1,500/night (a package that includes the boat and national-park fee), with an average review score of about 8.4 across several platforms · There are some things to know about the room condition before you book, though, and we've laid out what the real reviews say below.

body.html: The big picture and who it suits — say Koh Samet and most people picture the lively Sai Kaew Beach on the eastern shore, buzzing day and night · But cross to the other side of the island at Ao Prao on the west and the mood becomes something else entirely — a small, short, curving bay, quiet, with clear water, only a handful of resorts and most of them high-priced luxury places · Lima Coco Resort is a 3-star beach resort sitting right in the middle of Ao Prao Beach, and a clearly more affordable alternative to the luxury resorts on the same bay · What the real reviews agree on is the lovely, private beachfront setting, clear water you can snorkel coral in from the sand, friendly staff, and good food at prices that aren't steep next to the neighbouring resorts · It suits couples, small families and anyone who wants to escape the crowds and fall asleep to the waves without spending heavily, while still getting the Ao Prao that so many people are after · On the flip side, it isn't for anyone expecting luxury-hotel rooms, since some of the buildings and rooms are older and showing their age, and it isn't for the party crowd who want to wander at night or a choice of bars and restaurants, because Ao Prao is quiet and has almost nothing outside the resort · Put plainly, Lima Coco trades basic room condition for a lovely beach setting and a price you can actually reach — if you know what you're paying for, you're far less likely to be disappointed.

Location and getting there — first, an honest heads-up: Ao Prao isn't where the regular passenger ferries dock, and the trip in takes a little patience · From Bangkok it's about a 2.5–3 hour drive to Ban Phe pier in Rayong · From there, two main routes reach Ao Prao — the first is to take a boat to the Sai Kaew or Na Dan pier, then a songthaew across the island to Ao Prao, about another 3 km · The other is a speedboat straight into Ao Prao on certain departures · The thing to know is that many of the resort's packages already include the boat fare, the national-park fee and the on-island transfer, which saves you the hassle of arranging boats and rides yourself · It's worth confirming the boat times and pickup point with the resort before you reach the pier, as departures are limited and fill up fast in high season · The upside of a location like this is that once you're in the bay it feels like stepping into your own private world — no traffic, just waves and sea breeze · The trade-off that many reviews mention is that Ao Prao is fairly remote, and heading out for a meal or supplies is awkward, meaning a ride back across the island to the Sai Kaew side — if you can plan to eat and do your activities mostly within the resort, you'll have an easier time.

Rooms and decor — the resort has around 44 rooms, laid out as small Mediterranean-style villas in bright colours — reds, blues and yellows — climbing the shoulder of the hill above the bay · What sets this resort apart is that most rooms sit on the slope, so many of them get sea views from up high, looking down over the curving bay and a wide sweep of blue water · Rooms come in several tiers, from standard rooms of around 26 sqm up to sea-view rooms and rooms closer to the beach · In-room amenities cover the basics — air-conditioning, TV, fridge/minibar, kettle for tea and coffee, and a bathroom with hot water, and many rooms have a balcony out front to sit and take in the sea view · On the praise side, the real reviews say the sea-view rooms are worth it, the balcony really is a nice place to relax, and the air-con keeps things cool · But to be honest, this is where the reviews are most critical — many say the rooms and buildings look old and worn with age, some rooms are small and rather dark, lacking storage or a balcony, the hot water is sometimes unreliable with a wandering temperature, and a few bathrooms are poorly ventilated · Some reviews also note that the photos on the booking sites look better than the real thing · So if you're particular about room condition, choose a renovated sea-view room category and state your preferences when you book, so you don't set yourself up for disappointment.

"Open the balcony door to the sea and the soft sound of waves, walk a few steps down to the sand and you're snorkelling among fish — the setting and the view really are lovely, but the rooms look older than I expected. Anyone who's there for the view and the price will be happier than someone expecting a brand-new, spotless room." — drawn from the tone of real reviews across TripAdvisor and Agoda

Facilities, pool and activities — the highlight many people love about Lima Coco is the beachfront pool set looking out with the water of Ao Prao Bay as its backdrop · Late afternoon is the popular time, when guests go in for a soak, take photos and sit by the pool waiting for the sunset · There are beach loungers to lie out on all day · What really stands out is the activity off the sand — the water in front of Ao Prao is clear enough to see coral and shoals of fish from the beach, so you can snorkel and look at coral without taking a boat out · This is what clearly sets Ao Prao apart from the other beaches on Koh Samet, since many of them don't have clear water or coral close to shore · The resort also offers spa massages, bike rental, fishing trips and a tour desk · The overall vibe suits reading a book under the trees, sipping a cold drink by the pool, or strolling the beach in the evening · A selling point reviews mention often is that Ao Prao is one of the best sunset-viewing spots on Koh Samet, as the sun sinks slowly into the sea right in front of the bay — which is why many couples choose it to celebrate a special occasion · The honest observation is that beyond the sea and the pool, there isn't much else to do at the resort, so anyone restless or easily bored may feel there's little going on — this place sells quiet and rest above all.

Food and bar — the resort has a seaside restaurant and bar serving Thai food, international dishes and seafood · Dinner by the sea with the sunset is the image many reviews remember fondly, and some nights there's a fire-poi show on the beach · Several real reviews praise the food as tasty and reasonably priced next to the neighbouring resorts on the island, especially the seafood and Thai dishes, with a per-head spend in the mid-hundreds of baht · Breakfast is usually included in the package, with American-style, rice-porridge and Thai options to choose from · One thing that comes up repeatedly, though, is that service in the restaurant can be slow at times, especially when it's busy, and the menu isn't all that varied · Another thing to brace for is that, being on the island and a fairly remote bay, food and drink prices are naturally higher than on the mainland — normal for an island resort that has to ship everything across · Since Ao Prao has almost nothing outside the resort, eating at the resort is your main option, so anyone wanting to save might pack some snacks and drinking water from the mainland.

Service — service is a consistent bright spot in the real reviews · Many staff get a mention for being friendly, smiling, kind and attentive, especially around coordinating boat times, the on-island transfers and helping with activities · Plenty of people say that although the resort isn't luxurious, the warmth of the team makes it feel relaxed and welcoming · Cleanliness of the common areas, restaurant and beach earns decent marks · There are a few reviews that flag small things, such as wake-up calls or housekeeping arriving quite early on some days, and responses that aren't always consistent in the moment · On the whole it still feels like a small resort with an easy, informal touch rather than the polish of a big chain hotel — which for many people is the charm, not a downside.

What the real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulled together from TripAdvisor, Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com, and the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side, the most repeated points are the lovely, private Ao Prao Beach, clear water you can snorkel coral in from the sand, sea views from the hillside rooms and balconies, the beachfront pool, tasty and reasonably priced food, friendly and attentive staff, and the value next to the luxury resorts on the same bay · On the critical side, the recurring points are rooms and buildings that look old and worn with age, some rooms small and dark, lacking storage or a balcony, hot water that's sometimes unreliable, a few poorly ventilated bathrooms, booking-site photos that look better than reality, slow restaurant service at times, a trip in that means a boat and a ride, and a bay so quiet there's almost nothing to do but rest · On the review platforms Lima Coco Resort scores an average of around 8.4, and TripAdvisor ranks it around #8 of 24 hotels in Koh Samet, from over 336 reviews · The overall read is a resort that the people who love it love for the setting and the price, while those who come away disappointed usually expected a room condition higher than the price can deliver.

Price comparison and value — room rates at Lima Coco start at around ฿1,500/night for a standard room in a package that includes the boat, the national-park fee and the on-island transfer, rising to around two to three thousand baht for a sea-view room in high season or over a long weekend · This is the heart of the value — compared with Le Vimarn Cottages & Spa and Ao Prao Resort on the same Ao Prao Beach but several times the price and a notch more luxurious · Lima Coco gives you the same private beach, clear water and off-the-sand snorkelling, at a clearly lighter price · The trade-off you accept is the more basic, older room condition · Measured by a private beachfront setting and water this clear against the price you pay, it's very reasonable for anyone who weights location and budget over a luxurious room · But if you weight newness and room condition above all, paying more for a more recently renovated resort may feel like better value · The tip is to compare prices across platforms (Agoda, Booking, Trip.com) and check which package already includes the boat and breakfast, since the boat fare and park fee together add up to a fair amount.

What to know and tips before booking — one · Confirm the boat times and pickup point with the resort in advance, and check whether the package you booked already includes the boat fare, the national-park fee and the on-island transfer, or whether you pay those separately — this is where people slip up and get confused most often · Two · Choose a sea-view room category and ask for a renovated room in good condition, since the sea view from up high and an updated room are what make the rate worth it most, and it helps you avoid the small, dark or dated rooms · Three · Bring your own mask and snorkel, as there's coral and fish to see right off the sand and having your own gear is more convenient · Four · Pack mosquito repellent, drinking water and some snacks, since Ao Prao has nothing outside the resort and in-resort prices run higher than on the mainland · Five · if you're particular about hot water, mention it at check-in and ask them to check · Six · over long weekends and in high season (November–April), sea-view rooms and boat slots fill fast, so book several weeks ahead · Seven · set your expectations right from the start — come for the beach, the sea and the quiet, not for a luxury room, and the trip will be worth it and free of disappointment.

The bottom line — Lima Coco Resort is a good-value choice for anyone who wants to experience Ao Prao Beach on a lighter budget than the luxury resorts on the same bay · A quiet private beach, clear water you can snorkel coral in from the sand, a beachfront pool, and one of the best sunset-viewing spots on Koh Samet — all at a price you can reach · If you're a couple, a small family, or someone wanting to escape the crowds and fall asleep to the waves without paying a premium, this place delivers the rest you came for · You just have to accept the rooms and buildings being more basic and older than the luxury resorts, the trip in by boat and ride to the bay, and a quiet that may feel too lonely for the activity crowd · If you can take those three things, and you pick a sea-view room in good condition, Ao Prao will repay you with clear water and a quiet that's hard to find on Koh Samet these days, at a price plenty of people call better than expected.

honestSummary: Lima Coco Resort is a good-value choice on Ao Prao Beach for anyone who wants a private beach, clear water and quiet on a lighter budget than the luxury resorts on the same bay — snorkel coral off the sand, a beachfront pool, sunset views · You just have to accept the more basic, older rooms and buildings, and the trip in by boat and ride to the bay.
honestChecks: If you expect a brand-new, spotless luxury-hotel room — some buildings and rooms are old with age, and some rooms are small and dark → choose a sea-view room in good condition, or consider Ao Prao Resort / Le Vimarn on the same bay
If you want nightlife and a choice of restaurants to wander — Ao Prao is quiet and means crossing the island, with almost nothing outside the resort → a Sai Kaew-side hotel will be more convenient
If you're travelling over a long weekend or in high season (Nov–Apr) — sea-view rooms and boat slots fill fast → book ahead and confirm your boat time with the resort before you travel

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Lima Coco Resort, Koh Samet

faq.q: Which beach is Lima Coco Resort on, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's in the middle of Ao Prao Beach on the western shore of Koh Samet, which is quieter and more private than Sai Kaew · From Bangkok it's about a 3-hour drive to Ban Phe pier, then a boat across to the island and a ride over to Ao Prao, about another 3 km · Many of the resort's packages include the boat fare, the national-park fee and the transfer · Confirm the boat times with the resort in advance.

faq.q: How much does Lima Coco Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: From approx. ฿1,500/night for a Standard room in a package that includes the boat and national-park fee · Above that are Deluxe Sea View (sea view), Family Room and Beachfront Room closest to the sand · Prices depend on the season and package, so compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Lima Coco Resort, and anything to watch for?
faq.a: The rooms are colourful villas climbing the hillside with sea views, and cover the basic amenities · But several real reviews are critical that some buildings and rooms are old with age, some rooms are small and dark, the hot water is sometimes unreliable, and the website photos look newer than reality · We'd suggest choosing a sea-view room category and asking for a good-condition room when you book.

faq.q: Can you really snorkel coral off the beach at Lima Coco Resort?
faq.a: Yes · The highlight of Ao Prao is clear water with coral you can snorkel and see from the beach, without taking a boat out · Bringing your own mask/snorkel is more convenient.

faq.q: Who is Lima Coco Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples, small families and anyone wanting a quiet rest on Ao Prao Beach on a light budget · It's not for anyone expecting a brand-new, spotless luxury room, or anyone who wants nightlife and a choice of restaurants, since Ao Prao is quiet with almost nothing outside the resort.

faq.q: What is Lima Coco Resort's review score?
faq.a: An average of about 8.4 across several platforms · TripAdvisor ranks it around #8 of 24 hotels in Koh Samet, from over 336 reviews — reflecting that most guests like the beach, the quiet and the value, with some reservations about room condition.
